reason: The cited evidence supports that laser cladding is suitable for repairing high-value components (E3) and that HEAs have desirable properties (E1, E2), but no cited passage provides specific prior evidence for the key premises that laser-cladded HEA coatings avoid hot cracking, achieve the claimed property improvements, or that rapid solidification and multicomponent mixing produce the stated microstructural homogenization. The cited passages are only loosely related to the specific mechanistic and performance claims.
premises: Laser cladding provides confined, controlled heat input beneficial for repairing high-value components
High-entropy alloys (HEAs) can exhibit excellent mechanical properties and corrosion resistance
Laser cladding of HEAs can produce a refined, metallurgically bonded coating
Rapid solidification and multicomponent mixing in HEAs homogenize microstructure and avoid hot cracking
The proposed HEA coating will significantly outperform traditional fusion-welded repairs in hardness, wear, and corrosion resistance
